source.title: Relative Flatness and Generalization in the Interpolation Regime.
source.authors: Henning Petzka; Michael Kamp; Linara Adilova; Mario Boley; C. Sminchisescu

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: Measures relative flatness and generalization gaps in synthetic experiments and trained LeNet5 models, testing whether a flatness measure tracks the gap with a different measure from the claim's V7 magnitude-aware perturbation test.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own experiments relating flatness measures to generalization gaps. Training setups are used to obtain local minima; their individual outcomes are not separately reported as optimizer or batch-size comparisons. Cited results from other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests a Hessian-based relative-flatness measure, not V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance before training error rises. Its PAC-Bayes comparator is not identified as that specific measure. The other versions receive no direct tests.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors connect relative flatness to generalization under representativeness and approximately locally constant labels, report strong empirical correlations, and emphasize that violating the label condition can destroy the association.
record.recipe_differences: Measures Hessian-based relative flatness and its correlation with generalization gap, rather than magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness; synthetic data and LeNet5 on CIFAR10.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlation depends on whether labels are locally constant; the layer used for feature space changes its magnitude; reparameterization substantially lowers correlation for non-invariant measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative-flatness correlation increases with synthetic class separation and disappears without locally constant labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-based relative flatness predicts generalization conditionally on the label structure in feature space.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 110 converged LeNet5 solutions on CIFAR-10, relative flatness correlates more strongly with the generalization gap than the tested comparators.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative flatness can outperform the tested Hessian, Fisher-Rao, PAC-Bayes and weight-norm measures in predicting generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative flatness retains its correlation after layer rescaling and remains strongly correlated, though less strongly, at another fully connected layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative flatness is invariant to the tested layer rescalings, while its correlation strength depends on the feature layer.

record.problems: Experiments report correlations qualitatively in the supplied text without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The synthetic experiments use constructed data and 100 datasets per class separation; the CIFAR10 experiment reports only 110 local minima and excludes non-convergent hyperparameter combinations.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported row for each optimizer, batch size, or learning rate: those settings generated local minima for an aggregate correlation analysis, and the paper does not report their individual generalization-gap outcomes. No exact Figure 3–8 plotted values were reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required to fit.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Correlation and comparative ranking of the specified magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measure. Relative flatness measures a related property through a different mathematical quantity.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied versions; the paper does report qualitative outcomes for its own measure. Changing the measure does not itself justify partial states or limits_scope verdicts for V7.

versions.untested_parts: Whether models that fit random labels generalize on natural labels; natural versus random-label held-out performance.
Whether widening beyond the interpolation threshold lowers test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.

The paper tests correlations using relative flatness and several other measures; it does not test the version's magnitude-scaled weight perturbation measure, compare that measure with the listed norm and margin measures as specified, or test CIFAR-10 and SVHN without augmentation.
Removing the most memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: synthetic 5-layer MLP f = φ ◦ ψ
rows.size_stated: architecture 784-512-128-16-8 tanh feature extractor plus 8−2 output layer
rows.operation_detail: Measured relative flatness and generalization gap across synthetic datasets with varying class separation; authors report average correlation over 100 random datasets per separation.

conditions.value: synthetic binary classification in feature space

rows.measure: Correlation between relative flatness and generalization gap
rows.value: Figure 3 shows correlation increasing with degree of locally constant labels; if labels are not locally constant, flatness does not correlate with generalization.
rows.note: The paper reports the trend and qualitative null result, but gives no numeric correlation values in the supplied text.
rows.check: Synthetic correlations concern relative flatness, not V7's specified sharpness measure. The reported positive and null conditions should be separate rows if retained for a broader claim. The feature extractor is randomly initialized; only the linear predictor is fitted.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.operation_detail: Measured relative flatness and generalization gap at 110 local minima produced by varying learning rate, mini-batch size, initialization and optimizer; compared correlations with other measures.
rows.measure: Correlation of flatness measures with generalization gap
rows.baseline: Trace of loss Hessian, Fisher-Rao norm, PACBayes flatness measure, and L2 weight norm
rows.value: Relative flatness has higher correlation with generalization than all competing measures analyzed.
rows.locator: Section 6, Figure 5; Appendix C.2, Figures 6 and 8
rows.note: Correlations are described comparatively but exact numeric values are not stated in the text. Only convergent combinations were used; per-optimizer and per-batch outcomes are not reported separately.
rows.check: This reports the proposed relative-flatness measure outperforming comparators. It does not identify a result for magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness. Convergence means epoch loss below 0.1.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained until convergence; reparameterized after training
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation with generalization gap after layer-wise reparameterization using random factors in [5, 25].
rows.measure: Correlation of flatness measures with generalization gap after reparameterization
rows.value: Relative flatness and Fisher-Rao norm are invariant to reparameterization; correlation substantially declines for all other measures.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative comparison; no exact correlation values are stated.
rows.check: Relative-flatness invariance and declining correlations for other measures do not establish a result for V7's specified measure. The row combines several measures with different outcomes.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation of relative flatness on a fully connected layer other than the penultimate layer with generalization gap.

conditions.value: fully connected layer other than penultimate

rows.measure: Correlation between relative flatness and generalization gap
rows.baseline: Relative flatness measured using penultimate-layer feature space
rows.value: Correlation remains high, but the value is smaller than for the previous calculation.
rows.note: The text does not provide exact correlation values.
rows.check: Layer sensitivity concerns the proposed relative-flatness measure. A smaller correlation at another layer does not qualify V7's different measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic data with increasing class separation
reader_labels.reason: The reported correlation increases as labels become more locally constant (R1). This is a different flatness measure from the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic data without locally constant labels; LeNet5 reparameterizations and alternate feature layer
reader_labels.reason: Flatness does not correlate when labels are not locally constant; reparameterization reduces correlation for non-invariant measures, and the alternate layer has a smaller correlation (R1, R3, R4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LeNet5 on CIFAR10 across the reported local minima
reader_labels.reason: Relative flatness has higher correlation with the generalization gap than the tested competing measures (R2).
